- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5% for 30-day horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior 7-day avg), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) within 3–5 days, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply early mean-reversion bias: subtract 1–3% from forecast if sentiment drops below 0.3.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overfits recent volatility; use 14-day moving average as baseline to dampen short-term noise.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7), model tends to average or lag; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: higher sentiment → higher weight on recent prices, lower sentiment → weight on 14-day moving average.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a 30-day forecast, model often misses mean-reversion; add 1–3% downward bias if sentiment remains neutral or negative for 3+ days.
